definition: Model Interpretability concerns how clearly a model's predictions, parameters, or decisions can be understood by people. In AutoML, interpretability analysis helps compare pipelines and exposes which features, components, or hyperparameters drive behavior.
intuition: Interpretability asks what a model used and why a prediction changed, so performance claims can be checked against understandable behavior.
advantages: Can reveal feature reliance or pipeline behavior that aggregate scores hide.
Makes model behavior easier to audit, debug, and communicate.
limitations: An explanation can be locally useful without being a faithful global account of the model.
Interpretability methods can be unstable under correlated features or pipeline changes.
